context:
Measure first (w1), then place (w2) - do not default to a placement
before the runtime data exists. Reuse develop-post-merge.yml's existing
job pattern (checkout, setup-python, setup-uv, sync, run) rather than
inventing new plumbing. The w4 guardrail is the highest-leverage unit
here since it prevents recurrence of exactly this class of gap for any
future marker tier, not just medium - implement it regardless of which
placement w2 picks.
description:
81 test files carry `@pytest.mark.medium` (confirmed via
`grep -rl pytest.mark.medium tests/ | wc -l`), and `make test-medium`
(Makefile:90-91) is the only place that runs the full medium tier:
`-m "medium and not (slow or stress or resource_heavy or live_integration)"`.
No CI workflow invokes this Make target or an equivalent selector across
the full tier. The develop-PR gate's `code-test` job explicitly documents
that the fast-lane selection at pr.yml:450 (`-m "fast and not (...)"`)
skips medium-marked tests, and only pin-points two specific medium nodes
by name as explicit exceptions (pr.yml:419-424
`test_cross_surface_gates_are_pinned_in_make_and_ci`, and pr.yml:438-445
`test_plan_capture_phase.py`) - the comment at pr.yml:419 states this
outright: "Medium-marked ratchet, so the fast-lane selection below skips
it; invoke the node explicitly". `test.yml` (main-only, test.yml:3-9) also
does not select the medium marker as a tier - it has its own fast-lane
test job and separate `integration` job, neither of which is `-m medium`.
So the ~79 other medium-marked files run only when a developer runs
`make test-medium` locally; nothing in CI exercises them as a tier.

anti_patterns.dont: add `-m medium` selection into the existing required code-test job in pr.yml
anti_patterns.why: that inflates every develop PR's latency by the full tier's runtime regardless of what changed

anti_patterns.dont: remove or generalize away the two explicit medium-node pins at pr.yml:419-424/:438-445 as part of giving medium a general home
anti_patterns.instead: leave them as belt-and-suspenders duplication, not redundant work to clean up.
anti_patterns.why: their comments explain they were promoted early for specific regression reasons (#901, #909)

anti_patterns.dont: write the w4 guardrail as a hardcoded list of today's marker-to-workflow mappings that never re-derives from the workflow files
anti_patterns.instead: it must actually parse/grep the current workflow YAMLs and current marker set at test time.
anti_patterns.why: that check would pass even after this exact gap reappears for a new marker

preserves.behavior: The two explicit medium-node pins already in pr.yml (pr.yml:419-424, :438-445) stay in place even after the full tier gets a home - they are documented as deliberate early-promotion exceptions (pr.yml comments), not superseded by a general medium ring.

make test-medium's existing selector and worker count (`-n 5`, Makefile:90-91, asserted by test_makefile_test_medium_uses_five_workers) is unchanged - CI calls the same target, it does not reimplement the selector.
pr.yml's fast-lane PR gate keeps its current latency profile - do not fold the full medium tier into the required code-test job.

prior_art.concept: develop-post-merge.yml:20-56 lint/fast-test job pattern — reuse as the likely placement pattern
pr.yml:419-424, :438-445 explicit medium-node pin comments — reuse the '#issue-number promoted this specific regression' documentation style for any new guardrail comments

tests/unit/test_standardized_test_commands.py:271-287 test_makefile_test_medium_uses_five_workers / test_medium_marker_policy_is_documented_as_explicit_routing — reuse as the closest existing precedent for the w4 guardrail's shape

work_units.notes:
Done. Ran the exact command:
`time uv run -- python -m pytest tests -m "medium and not (slow or
stress or resource_heavy or live_integration)" -q -p no:cacheprovider`
(note: no `-n 5`, unlike `make test-medium` itself — this session was
given that exact command to run, not the Makefile target, so the
worker count came from pytest.ini's default rather than the Makefile's
explicit `-n 5`; the harness capped xdist workers from "auto" to 2 in
this sandbox — see "[benchbox] Capped pytest-xdist workers from auto
to 2" in the run log).

RESULT: 1070.38s wall clock (~17.85 min), 1158 passed, 73 skipped, 15
failed, 44 errors. Well past "fast-lane-comparable" and squarely in
the TODO's own "10+ minutes -> nightly or post-merge" bucket.

FAILURE BREAKDOWN (important caveat below): the ONE failure this TODO
pre-flagged as known/expected was present as predicted:
`tests/unit/test_cross_surface_applicability.py::test_committed_artifact_is_current`.
Per this TODO's own instruction, I did NOT fix or regenerate that
artifact and did NOT exclude the test — see w2 notes for how the new
lane's known-issue is documented instead.

However 14 OTHER failures and 44 errors also occurred, which this
TODO did not anticipate:
  - tests/unit/test_error_handling.py::test_permission_denied_output_directory,
    ::test_readonly_filesystem_handling; tests/unit/cli/test_exceptions.py::
    test_validate_output_directory_local_invalid — these are classic
    "running pytest as root" artifacts: chmod-based permission-denial
    tests cannot produce PermissionError when the test process is
    root, which ignores file-mode permission bits. Root cause is this
    sandbox's execution user, not this session's edits.
  - tests/integration/test_dataframe_adapter_smoke.py (8 PySpark
    tests) — failed rather than cleanly skipped, alongside dozens of
    other PySpark tests elsewhere in the same run that DID skip
    cleanly with "Java not found" — suggests a partial/inconsistent
    JVM install in this sandbox, not a code regression.
  - tests/integration/validation/test_read_primitives_variant_parity.py
    (44 ERRORs, all in one file, spanning duckdb/datafusion/redshift/
    clickhouse reference-output fixtures) — the uniform failure shape
    across many parametrized cases in a single file is consistent
    with a fixture/session-level setup exception, and this session
    was running OTHER pytest invocations concurrently against the
    same tree with BENCHBOX_SKIP_TEST_LOCK=1 (bypassing this repo's
    own single-run lock) while this measurement was in flight, plus a
    second agent was independently running pytest against this same
    shared worktree at the same time (per the task's own instructions
    — this tree is explicitly shared with another concurrent agent).
    Concurrent DB-file/port/tmp-dir contention is a plausible cause.
  - tests/unit/cli/test_output_control_static.py::test_no_new_raw_print_in_benchbox_runtime
    — a static source-grep test; not obviously environment-related,
    and not touched by this session's edits (no benchbox/ source
    changed). Cause undetermined.

I could NOT re-run in isolation to separate "real develop regression"
from "sandbox/concurrency artifact" within this session's time budget
(a clean rerun takes ~18 min and this session had already produced
the required measurement). RECOMMENDATION: before relying on the new
develop-post-merge auto-revert wiring in production (see w2/w3), a
human or follow-up session should run `make test-medium` once, alone,
in a clean environment (ideally the actual GitHub Actions runner) to
get a trustworthy failure baseline. If the 14+44 are confirmed
environment noise, no code changes are needed; if any are real
regressions, they need their own fix TODOs before the auto-revert
wiring can be trusted not to fire spuriously. Original notes:
Run `time make test-medium` and record wall-clock time and pass/fail
count. This number drives w2's placement choice - a lane under a few
minutes is a candidate for a path-filtered PR job; a lane of 10+
minutes is a better fit for nightly or post-merge.

work_units.notes:
DECISION: develop-post-merge.yml (the TODO's own default, and w1's
~18-minute runtime confirms it — nowhere close to fast-lane-comparable
or PR-blocking viable). Added a `medium-test` job to
develop-post-merge.yml mirroring the lint/fast-test job shape
(checkout, setup-python 3.12, setup-uv, sync, run), calling `make
test-medium` directly (no new Make target, per w3). Gave it
`timeout-minutes: 30` (measured ~18 min + headroom).

REVISED AFTER REVIEW (2026-07-04): the job initially landed fully
wired into the auto-revert path (needs + if OR-condition), but review
correctly flagged that the tier has at least one known-red test on
clean develop (test_committed_artifact_is_current) plus 14
undispositioned failures / 44 errors from the contended measurement
(see w1) — so the first innocent merge after landing would have fired
an auto-revert PR against an unrelated change. DECOUPLED: medium-test
stays in develop-post-merge.yml for visibility/metrics but now has
`continue-on-error: true` and is EXCLUDED from
`auto-revert-on-failure.needs` and its `if:` trigger. A tier failure
shows red in the run's job list without opening a revert PR.

PROMOTION CRITERION (recorded in the medium-test job comment and
pinned by tests/unit/workflows/test_develop_post_merge_metrics.py::
test_medium_test_is_visibility_only_not_auto_revert_trigger): promote
to a real auto-revert trigger only after a FULL CLEAN (green) run of
the medium tier. Prerequisites: (1) regenerate the stale
cross-surface-applicability committed artifact (own TODO/fix, not
this one), and (2) a clean-environment re-measurement to disposition
the other 14 failures / 44 errors (real regressions get their own fix
TODOs; environment noise needs no code change). Promotion is
mechanical: drop continue-on-error, add medium-test back to
auto-revert-on-failure's needs + if (mirror lint/fast-test), and flip
the pinned demotion test to the explorer-tokens-style assertions.

Metrics wiring KEPT but currently inert: `MEDIUM_TEST_RESULT` in the
metrics job env, the shell `post_merge_red` boolean, and the `$red_at`
jq filter all still reference medium-test, but with job-level
continue-on-error `needs.medium-test.result` reads "success" even on
failure, so none of them can fire until promotion — at which point
they become live automatically with zero metrics-side churn (verified
not to break: the metrics job runs `if: always()` and its needs list
keeps medium-test so the env expression resolves). Pinned tests in
tests/unit/workflows/test_develop_post_merge_metrics.py updated:
RED_AT_JQ fixture + shell-flag/jq tests kept (with inert-while-demoted
comments), the auto-revert-trigger test replaced by the demotion pin.

Deliberately did NOT add medium-test to `close-orphaned-prs.needs`
(pinned exactly to [lint, fast-test, explorer-tokens] by
test_close_orphaned_prs_waits_for_post_merge_validation_success) —
that automation doesn't depend on medium-test's result and adding an
18-minute job to its wait chain would delay orphan-PR cleanup for no
correctness benefit. Original notes:
Three placement options, pick one based on w1:
  - develop-post-merge.yml: add a `medium-test` job calling
    `make test-medium`, non-blocking to the PR but caught
    immediately post-merge via the existing auto-revert path
    (mirrors the `lint`/`fast-test` jobs, develop-post-merge.yml:20-56).
  - nightly.yml matrix: add `make test-medium` as a job/step alongside
    the existing `integration-smoke` matrix.
  - path-filtered PR job in pr.yml: only viable if w1's runtime is
    fast-lane-comparable; otherwise this adds meaningful PR latency
    to every code-touching PR since the medium tier is not narrowly
    scoped to one path group.
Default to develop-post-merge.yml unless w1's runtime data argues
otherwise - it is the option most consistent with keeping the PR gate
fast while still catching regressions within one merge.

work_units.notes:
Done. Added `test_every_speed_marker_tier_has_a_ci_consumer` to
tests/unit/test_standardized_test_commands.py (that file's existing
scope — Makefile/CI-pinning assertions — was the closer fit than
test_marker_strategy.py, which asserts marker-hygiene on test files
themselves, not CI wiring). It derives the known marker set from
`tests.unit.test_marker_strategy._SPEED_MARKERS |
_E2E_QUICK_INCOMPATIBLE` (fast, medium, slow, stress, resource_heavy,
live_integration) — not a hardcoded list in the new test itself — and
greps (word-boundary regex, not naive substring) the combined text of
pr.yml, test.yml, nightly.yml, and develop-post-merge.yml, failing if
any marker has zero references across all four.

CAVEAT on the guardrail's actual sensitivity (worth flagging
honestly): because `medium` already had 3 references in pr.yml before
this TODO (the two explicit early-promotion node pins at pr.yml
:419-424/:438-445, which this TODO's must_preserve/anti-pattern
explicitly says to keep), this guard was ALREADY passing before w2's
medium-test job existed, and would ALSO still pass if the new
develop-post-merge medium-test job were later removed (the two
existing pins still reference the marker). So the TODO's own w4
verification bullet ("temporarily commenting out the medium job in
the CI workflow makes it fail") does not hold exactly for the
`medium` marker specifically, given those pre-existing pins — the
guard is a genuine, code-derived (not hardcoded) trip-wire for a
marker that loses ALL CI references, which is the literal spec given,
but it is not sensitive enough to detect "the FULL tier's dedicated
job was removed while narrow pins remain." A stronger version would
need to specifically require the tier's `make test-<marker>`
invocation (or an equivalent whole-tier `-m` selector) to appear, not
just any reference to the marker name — that would be a fair
follow-up refinement, not implemented here since the TODO's spec
("greps the known speed markers ... fails if any marker has zero
references") was implemented literally. Original notes:
Find the right home in `tests/unit/test_standardized_test_commands.py`
(which already has Makefile/CI-pinning assertions, e.g.
`test_cross_surface_gates_are_pinned_in_make_and_ci` and
`test_makefile_test_medium_uses_five_workers` at :271-278) or
`tests/unit/test_marker_strategy.py` (which already asserts marker
hygiene, e.g. `test_tree_has_no_fast_or_medium_decorators`,
`test_routine_test_modules_have_a_single_top_level_speed_marker`) -
whichever file's existing scope is the closer fit. Add a test that
greps the known speed markers (fast, medium, slow, stress,
resource_heavy, live_integration) against the CI workflow YAMLs
(pr.yml, test.yml, nightly.yml, develop-post-merge.yml) and fails if
any marker has zero references across all four files. This is the
guardrail that prevents this exact gap (a tier silently losing every
CI consumer) from recurring undetected.
work_units.summary: Add a lint/unit check asserting every speed-marker tier has at least one CI consumer
